messages.content: I want to buy apples, rice, and 12 pack of bottled water from a Walmart near San Jose. Show me the product information and stock availability.

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

message.reasoning: We need to call the function walmart_purchase with loc "San Jose" or "near San Jose". product_list ["apples", "rice", "bottled water"] pack_size [12] for bottled water? Actually pack_size array length equal to product_list. So we need pack_size for each product. For apples and rice, no pack size. We can set pack_size as [] or maybe null. The function signature says pack_size?: number[]. So optional. But if we provide pack_size, it should match length of product_list. We could provide pack_size [null, null, 12] but type is number[]. So maybe we omit pack_size entirely. But then we can't specify 12 pack. Maybe we can include pack_size [12] only for bottled water? But array length must equal product_list. So we need to provide pack_size [0,0,12] or something. But better to omit pack_size and rely on default. But requirement: "12 pack of bottled water". So we need to specify pack_size for bottled water. So we can provide pack_size [12] but length mismatch. The function spec says "The size of the array should be equal to product_list." So we must provide pack_size array of same length. So we can provide pack_size [1,1,12] meaning 1 pack for apples and rice? That doesn't make sense. Maybe we can provide pack_size [null, null, 12] but type number[] prohibits null. Could use 0 for apples and rice. Let's do pack_size [0,0,12]. That indicates no pack size for apples and rice. We'll call function.
